## Test one document only

This tests whether table-related headers are bleeding into adjacent text sections.

```{python}

import os
import zipfile
import pandas as pd
from docx import Document
from lxml import etree

# =====================================================
# TEST DOCUMENT
# =====================================================

doc_path = "no_tables_AK/16901_68.docx"

# =====================================================
# OUTPUT DIRECTORY
# =====================================================

output_directory = "tables_AK_test"

os.makedirs(output_directory, exist_ok=True)

# =====================================================
# SECTIONS TO EXTRACT
# =====================================================

sections = [
    "Vegetation Type",
    "Map Zones",
    "Model Splits or Lumps",
    "Geographic Range",
    "Biophysical Site Description",
    "Vegetation Description",
    "Disturbance Description",
    "Scale Description",
    "Adjacency or Identification Concerns",
    "Issues or Problems",
    "Native Uncharacteristic Conditions",
    "Comments",
    "References"
]

# =====================================================
# HEADERS THAT SHOULD STOP EXTRACTION
# =====================================================

stop_headers = [
    "Vegetation Type",
    "Map Zones",
    "Model Splits or Lumps",
    "Geographic Range",
    "Biophysical Site Description",
    "Vegetation Description",
    "BpS Dominant and Indicator Species",
    "Disturbance Description",
    "Fire Frequency",
    "Scale Description",
    "Adjacency or Identification Concerns",
    "Issues or Problems",
    "Native Uncharacteristic Conditions",
    "Comments",
    "Succession Classes",
    "References"
]

stop_headers_lower = [x.lower() for x in stop_headers]

# =====================================================
# EXTRACT SECTIONS
# =====================================================

def extract_sections(doc_path, sections):

    doc = Document(doc_path)

    paragraphs = [
        p.text.replace("\xa0", " ").strip()
        for p in doc.paragraphs
        if p.text.strip() != ""
    ]

    content_dict = {sec: None for sec in sections}

    for i, para in enumerate(paragraphs):

        for section in sections:

            if para.lower() == section.lower():

                content = []

                for j in range(i + 1, len(paragraphs)):

                    current_text = paragraphs[j].strip().lower()

                    if current_text in stop_headers_lower:
                        break

                    content.append(paragraphs[j])

                text = "\n".join(content).strip()

                content_dict[section] = text if text else None

    content_dict["document"] = os.path.basename(doc_path)

    return content_dict

# =====================================================
# EXTRACT DOC METADATA
# =====================================================

def extract_core_properties(doc_path):

    with zipfile.ZipFile(doc_path, "r") as docx:

        with docx.open("docProps/core.xml") as core_xml:

            tree = etree.parse(core_xml)

            ns = {
                "cp": "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/metadata/core-properties",
                "dc": "http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/",
                "dcterms": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/"
            }

            return {
                "creator":
                    tree.findtext(
                        "cp:coreProperties/dc:creator",
                        namespaces=ns
                    ),
                "lastModifiedBy":
                    tree.findtext(
                        "cp:coreProperties/cp:lastModifiedBy",
                        namespaces=ns
                    ),
                "revision":
                    tree.findtext(
                        "cp:coreProperties/cp:revision",
                        namespaces=ns
                    ),
                "created":
                    tree.findtext(
                        "cp:coreProperties/dcterms:created",
                        namespaces=ns
                    ),
                "modified":
                    tree.findtext(
                        "cp:coreProperties/dcterms:modified",
                        namespaces=ns
                    )
            }

# =====================================================
# RUN TEST
# =====================================================

sections_data = extract_sections(doc_path, sections)
core_props_data = extract_core_properties(doc_path)

df = pd.DataFrame([{**sections_data, **core_props_data}])

# use same name as source docx

doc_name = os.path.splitext(
    os.path.basename(doc_path)
)[0]

output_file = os.path.join(
    output_directory,
    f"{doc_name}.csv"
)

df.to_csv(output_file, index=False)

print("\n===================================")
print("DOCUMENT:")
print(df["document"][0])

print("\n===================================")
print("VEGETATION DESCRIPTION")
print(df["Vegetation Description"][0])

print("\n===================================")
print("DISTURBANCE DESCRIPTION")
print(df["Disturbance Description"][0])

print("\n===================================")
print("COMMENTS")
print(df["Comments"][0])

print("\n===================================")
print("CSV WRITTEN TO:")
print(output_file)

```
